architecture: EfficientNetB0 (frozen ImageNet base) -> GAP -> Dense(128) -> Dropout(0.3) -> Dense(1, sigmoid)
dataset: BTX24/PCOS-ultrasound-dataset (Hugging Face mirror of the Kaggle PCOS ultrasound data)
limitations: Research prototype — metrics are NOT evidence of PCOS detection ability. A non-anatomical baseline (image size and brightness only) reaches AUROC 1.000 on the same held-out split, showing the two class folders differ by acquisition source rather than only by anatomy. The dataset also has no patient identifiers, so splits are image-level and frames from one patient may span splits. Not clinically validated, not a medical device, and not a diagnosis.

non_anatomical_baseline.features: image width, height, area, aspect ratio, mean brightness, brightness sd

shortcut_audit.interpretation: A model using only image geometry and brightness — no anatomy at all — reaches AUROC 1.000 on the same held-out split. The two class folders therefore differ systematically in acquisition/processing (resolution and brightness), so the CNN's near-perfect score is explained by that shortcut rather than by detecting ovarian morphology. These metrics must NOT be presented as evidence of PCOS detection ability or of real-world performance.
